text:
maria: quick question — i'm sketching a refactor to split the orchestration stack. currently everything's in one "coordinator" binary. thinking of an explicit coordinator (global scheduler) vs controller (per-pool node agent) split. where should eviction/headroom semantics live?

aj: my take: coordinator owns long-term policy (quota, fairness, global headroom), controller owns immediate decisions (probe, soft-evict when node overloaded). coordinator gives hints, controller enforces SLOs.

devon: agree with aj. main gotcha is race conditions: two controllers evicting the same tenant because coordinator hasn't reconciled. need idempotent leasing / short lease tokens.

samira: +1. also telemetry surface matters. coordinator needs per-tenant demand curves (rps, seq len) to make allocation decisions. controllers should only emit lightweight signals, not full traces.

maria: concretely: proposal sketch below. controller receives a lease token from coordinator with expiry and metadata. controller may preempt soft reservations if local pressure > threshold, but must report action back with backoff window.

maria: ```json
{
  "lease": "L-12345",
  "owner_tenant": "tenant-42",
  "expires_at": "2024-11-12T15:02:00Z",
  "headroom": 2,
  "policy": "soft-reserve"
}
```

lee: sounds reasonable. question: where do we evaluate cost tradeoffs (quantize batching vs spinup)? coordinator has global cost model, but controller has better locality info (cv of startup times). maybe we let controller compute a local adj factor and report it periodically. coordinator multiplies by that factor for admission planning.

aj: yeah, local_adjustment is good. keep math simple on coordinator side: effective_headroom = announced_headroom * local_adj

infra-bot: deploy-check: coordinator-api v2 will add field `local_adj` to LeaseStatus. Please bump compatibility.

devon: another operational concern: upgrades. if controller is temporarily lagging, we shouldn't have coordinator push hard decisions that controllers can't enforce. need a degraded-mode where coordinator falls back to capacity-based admission (no evictions).

samira: op note: add an observable: "controller_evicts_total" with labels {tenant, reason, preemptible}. that will let us catch incorrect coordinator policies.

maria: timeline idea: land coordinator read-only surface first (expose leases, signals), then controller implements enforcement in canary pool. run for 2 weeks with canaries before turning on coordinator-initiated evictions.

aj: one more nit: naming. call the short-lived node agent "controller" and the global decision engine "coordinator"? feels confusing. maybe call global "planner" and node agent "agent". simple names reduce cognitive overhead. :+1:

maria: good catch. i'll rename in RFC draft to planner vs agent.

lee: 👍 also add a simple JSON example of degraded-mode in the RFC: { "mode": "degraded", "reason": "controller-mismatch" }

maria: summary action items:
- switch naming -> planner/agent in RFC draft
- add lease token example + local_adj field (aj)
- add controller_evicts_total metric + alert (samira)
- propose canary rollout plan (maria)

aj: +1 to everything. tagging @devon for the idempotent lease implementation follow-up.

devon: i'll draft the idempotent lease proto and a small test harness that simulates split-brain evictions. aim for PR by EOW.

maria: perfect. thanks everyone. closing thread after the RFC update. :rocket:
